reviews: Bound event-time work by elements as well as text; avoid full child collection allocation; keep one owned notice and timer.
Preserve ordinary downloads and player controls, restrict loose ad labels to nearby ancestors, validate settings migration and sender-derived exceptions with rollback.
Verify native event ordering and fresh trusted feedback, frame/navigation lifecycle, package consumers, narrow UI, final hashes and documentation.
baseline: Before the guard, the marked advertising Download button reached early page handlers and fragment navigation in Chrome.
fixtureFindings: Firefox Picture-in-Picture browser UI intercepted centered video-overlay input without page events. Final fixtures target the page link away from that native control and require fresh trusted feedback on every gesture.

The permitted same-site overlay retained target=_blank in an early fixture. Final same-tab fixture removes target; a separate ordinary external Download link explicitly verifies allowed new-tab navigation.
Diagnostic event traces existed only in disposable test copies; final packages have no trace instrumentation.
One fresh Chrome run timed out awaiting initial popup state without a reported runtime error. The full rerun passed with unchanged assertions; the startup cause was not established.
limits: Conservative local patterns, not universal fake-button detection or a malware/file scanner; no live scam sites tested.
Unknown labels, unmarked controls, closed shadow roots, earlier handlers, rewritten destinations and deliberate evasion may escape detection.
Browser-owned UI, context-menu navigation, manually entered URLs, hover actions and native touch devices are outside the demonstrated coverage.
No desktop helper permission prompts or real notifications were exercised; the normal browser download fixture saves only an owned CSV.
